Ask again with the labels in another order

order_sensitivity.Rd

Measures every document again, or a seeded sample of them, with the labels shown in reverse and, on three or more labels, in one shuffled order, and compares the answers with the ones the run already holds. Every call in a run sees the labels in the order the instrument declared, so nothing in the run can show whether that order moved its answers.

A prompt shows the labels in order in two places, the cue and, on an exclusive instrument, the listing of definitions under the question. Both are rebuilt for each order. Matching and any probed tokens carry over by label name rather than being probed again, so only the presentation moves.

Usage

order_sensitivity(
  results,
  docs = NULL,
  ...,
  text = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  image = NULL,
  items = NULL,
  n = NULL,
  level = c("nominal", "ordinal"),
  labels = NULL,
  ci = c("none", "bootstrap"),
  conf_level = 0.95,
  bootstrap_n = 2000L,
  seed = 1234L
)

Arguments

results

A fathom_results object from measure() or read_checkpoints(). It supplies the instrument, the backend and the context ceiling the calls are made with.

docs

A character vector, or the data frame passed to measure(). Default is NULL, which uses the documents a character-vector run stored on the results.

...

Not used, and refused if anything reaches it. Every argument after it is name-only, so a misspelling lands here rather than being matched by position.

text, id

Strings naming the text and identifier columns, if docs is a data frame. id defaults to the row position, as in measure(). text may be left out when image is given and the run sent no text.

image

A string naming the column in docs that holds each document's media, as passed to measure(). A run that sent media needs it here too, or every call asks about a prompt the run never sent. Default is NULL.

items

A character vector restricting the audit to specific items, or NULL (the default) for all of them.

n

An integer giving the documents drawn per item, from those with a label in the run, or NULL to ask about all of them. An item with fewer than n uses all it has. Default is NULL. Drawing 50 puts the standard error of an agreement near 0.9 at about 0.04.

level

A string, "nominal" (the default) or "ordinal", deciding how alpha charges a disagreement, as in validate_sample().

labels

A character vector giving, under "ordinal", every label in scale order. Ignored under "nominal". Default is NULL, which takes the order from the instrument's scores.

ci

A string choosing whether to report intervals. "none", the default, returns none and the interval columns are absent. "bootstrap" adds one bracketed column beside agreement and alpha.

conf_level

A number giving the coverage of every interval, 0.95 by default. It is stamped on the result as the conf_level attribute.

bootstrap_n

An integer giving the replicates for each interval. The default is a round two thousand, and below a hundred is refused.

seed

An integer giving the seed for the shuffled order, the draw and the intervals, so the same call asks about the same documents. The session's random stream is put back on exit. NULL draws from the session's stream instead. Default is 1234.

Value

A tibble with one row per item and order, items in instrument order and "reversed" before "shuffled". The label sequences are on the orders attribute, the declared one first, and in the printed header.

  • item is the question name.

  • order is "reversed", or "shuffled" on three or more labels.

  • n counts the documents compared, those where the reordered call returned a label. A call that failed or returned none is left out and warned about, since an order that pushes the answer off the labels is itself an effect of the order.

  • agreement is the share of those documents whose winning label is the same under both orders.

  • alpha is Krippendorff's alpha with the two orders as two coders of the same documents. On two labels the nominal and ordinal metrics coincide.

level and conf_level are stamped as attributes, and run_at and call as on the other objects here.

What it costs

The declared order is read off results, so it costs no calls. Each other order costs one call per document asked about. The default asks about every document with a label, so the cost grows with the corpus. A number for n caps it, and n = 50 makes it 50 calls an item on two labels and 100 on three or more.

The instrument, the backend and the context ceiling all come off results, so the calls run under the model and settings of the run being audited. Nothing is checkpointed, and the run's checkpoint directory is never touched. A reordered prompt hashes differently, so a call stored there would mark the item stale and replace the run's rows with the audit's.

A cue written by hand

The package does not rewrite wording it did not write. An exclusive instrument with its own cue keeps it, and only its listing is reordered. An instrument of items lists its labels nowhere but the cue, so with its own cue there is nothing to reorder and the call is refused.

See also

threshold_sensitivity() for the other choice a measurement should not depend on, where the cut falls, and validate_sample() for agreement with a human rather than with the model itself.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Needs a running Ollama server, so it is not run here.
p <- system.file("extdata", "vignette_results.rds", package = "fathom")
baked <- readRDS(p)
order_sensitivity(baked$res_indep, parlasent, text = "sentence", id = "id")
} # }
